name: NASA POWER
purpose: Daily weather for the place since 1981: high and low temperature, rain, sunlight, dew point, humidity and wind. Every climate chart and trend, the hot, dry and frost windows, reference evapotranspiration, and so the water fit and heat scores are worked out from it. In the answers the tool has received, sunlight is missing before 1984, so reference evapotranspiration starts in 1984.
resolution: Roughly 35 miles across (about 55 km) for weather values, on a grid of ½° latitude by ⅝° longitude. Sunlight values are on a coarser grid of 1° by 1°.
confidence: Medium: regional climate, not a field station

name: USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer
purpose: The crop at the chosen point in each of the last 8 years, read through USDA's Cropland Data Layer image service. The field's own rotation is built from those years, and any year can be corrected by hand.
confidence: High; single-pixel misclassification is possible, so the farmer can edit

name: USDA NRCS SSURGO soil survey
purpose: The soil map unit under the point, read through Soil Data Access: the texture, organic matter, K factor, wind erodibility index and hydrologic group of its main soil, and the available water and slope of the whole unit. It sets how much water the soil can store for the next crop and the erosion risk behind the soil protection score.
confidence: High for soil type; the map unit can still mix soils

name: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Crop Evapotranspiration (Allen, Pereira, Raes and Smith, 1998)

links.label: Chapter 6, crop coefficients and stage lengths

purpose: The method for reference evapotranspiration (the Penman-Monteith equation), and the crop coefficients and growth-stage lengths behind each crop's potential water demand. It is a worldwide handbook: none of the stage-length rows the tool uses is labelled for Kansas (they are for Idaho, for Spain and California, for the USA, Pakistan and the Mediterranean, and for the central USA), so their lengths are scaled to the Kansas season.

name: U.S. EPA, Guidance for Data Quality Assessment: Practical Methods for Data Analysis (EPA QA/G-9, QA00 update, July 2000)
purpose: The trend methods: the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, and what a regression slope assumes (section 4.3).

links.label: The layer, as NASA describes it

purpose: The vegetation layer that can be switched on over the map: the vegetation index (NDVI) from the MODIS instrument on NASA's Terra satellite, about one picture every 16 days since March 2000, on a schedule that starts again each 1 January (NASA's product MOD13Q1). The browser loads the pictures straight from NASA. It is a picture only: no score uses it.
resolution: About 820 ft (250 m) at its sharpest, straight below the satellite

name: OpenFreeMap, Positron style

name: U.S. Census Bureau, TIGERweb

links.label: The query the rectangle came from

purpose: The rectangle around Kansas that the map opens on and that the tool uses to decide whether a point is inside the state. It is a rectangle, not the state line, so ground just outside Kansas can pass where the border is not straight. Also the outline of each of the 105 counties, simplified, from which the tool finds the county a point is in for its soil moisture record (public/data/counties.geojson, written by scripts/kansas_county_outlines.py).

name: NASA SMAP

links.label: SMAP Enhanced L3 soil moisture, version 6 (NSIDC)
NASA AppEEARS, where the county samples were read
The layers AppEEARS lists for the product, with their valid range
AppEEARS's decoding of the quality flag

purpose: Soil moisture in roughly the top 5 cm (2 inches) of soil, as a share of the soil's volume, read by the SMAP satellite's radiometer on its morning pass (about 6 a.m. local solar time), daily since 31 March 2015. A script asked NASA AppEEARS for the daily values at the center of each of the 105 Kansas counties, and the app holds one small file per county: the average of each month, and the last full month set against the same month in the other years. It is shown as a status, wetter or drier than usual. No score uses it.
resolution: A 9 km grid cell (about 5.6 miles across), interpolated from a radiometer footprint of about 36 km (22 miles). The tool reads the cell at the center of the county, so the figure is the county's, not the field's.
confidence: Medium: an area average, not one field

name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center

links.label: Forecast tools: how above, near and below normal are defined

purpose: How the Center defines above, near and below normal: the thirds of a climatological distribution. The tool borrows the thirds, by analogy, for its soil moisture label.
